title: CLAUDE.md – wehoop Development Guide
text: wehoop R package providing clean, tidy women’s basketball play--play box score data. wraps WNBA Stats API, ESPN API (WNBA & WBB), NCAA women’s basketball endpoints, exporting 200+ functions across multiple data source families: wnba_*(), espn_wnba_*(), espn_wbb_*(), ncaa_wbb_*(). guide differs current repository docs, treat CONTRIBUTING.md current test implementations authoritative. Version: 3.0.0 (dev) R Requirement: >= 4.1.0 License: MIT Branch: main default branch release branch.

title: CLAUDE.md – wehoop Development Guide
text: WNBA Stats API NCAA wrappers historically use @details--fenced-code-block pattern runnable examples. Example: @details--code-block style applies WNBA Stats API NCAA wrappers, ’s preserved backward compatibility legacy 2.x documentation surface.
code: #' **Get WNBA Stats API [Endpoint Name]** #' @name wnba_functionname NULL #' @title #' **Get WNBA Stats API [Endpoint Name]** #' @rdname wnba_functionname #' @author Saiem Gilani #' @param game_id Game ID - 10-digit zero-padded ID (e.g., '1022200034') #' @param ... Additional arguments passed to an underlying function like httr. #' @return Returns a named list of data frames: Component1, Component2 #' #'    **Component1** #' #'    |col_name |types     | #'    |:--------|:---------| #'    |column1  |character | #' #' @importFrom jsonlite fromJSON toJSON #' @importFrom dplyr filter select rename bind_cols bind_rows as_tibble #' @import rvest #' @export #' @family WNBA Boxscore V3 Functions #' @details #' ```r #'  wnba_functionname(game_id = "1022200034") #' ``` wnba_functionname <- function(game_id = "1022200034", ...) {   endpoint <- wnba_endpoint('endpointname')   full_url <- endpoint   params <- list(GameID = pad_id(game_id))    df_list <- list()  # Always initialize before tryCatch    tryCatch(     expr = {       resp <- request_with_proxy(url = full_url, params = params, ...)       # Parse response...       # Apply janitor::clean_names()       # Apply make_wehoop_data()     },     error = function(e) {       cli::cli_alert_danger("{Sys.time()}: Invalid arguments or no data for {game_id} available!")       cli::cli_alert_danger("Error:\n{e}")     },     warning = function(w) {       cli::cli_alert_warning("{Sys.time()}: Warning:\n{w}")     },     finally = {}   )   return(df_list) }

text: ESPN wrappers (espn_wbb_*, espn_wnba_*) use standard CRAN-conforming @examples block instead. Live-API examples wrapped \donttest{} R CMD check hit ESPN routine checking, still exercised --run-donttest. mix two styles – ESPN wrappers never carry @details code-block example. ESPN public wrappers thin shims internal helpers R/espn_basketball_*_helpers.R take league argument ("wnba" "womens-college-basketball"). helpers actual HTTP call + parsing; public functions just fix league slug. keeps WBB/WNBA pair DRY – one bugfix helper propagates public wrappers. ESPN wrappers use ESPN-side reporters .report_api_error(e, hint, args) .report_api_warning(w, args) (R/utils.R), captured function entry .args <- mget(setdiff(names(formals()), "...")) (.args <- .capture_args() argless wrappers). use raw cli::cli_alert_danger() – WNBA Stats convention.
code: #' **Get ESPN [Endpoint Name]** #' @name espn_wbb_functionname NULL #' @title #' **Get ESPN [Endpoint Name]** #' @rdname espn_wbb_functionname #' @author Saiem Gilani #' @param team_id ESPN team identifier (character or numeric). #' @param season Season year. Defaults to `most_recent_wbb_season()`. #' @param ... Reserved for forward compatibility. Per-call proxy override is #'   not supported for ESPN wrappers; use `getOption("wehoop.proxy")` or the #'   `http_proxy`/`https_proxy` environment variables. #' @return A `wehoop_data` tibble with one row per ... . #' #'    |col_name |types     | #'    |:--------|:---------| #'    |column1  |character | #' #' @importFrom jsonlite fromJSON #' @importFrom dplyr select as_tibble any_of #' @importFrom janitor clean_names #' @export #' @family ESPN WBB Functions #' @examples #' \donttest{ #'   espn_wbb_functionname(team_id = "2509", season = 2025) #' } espn_wbb_functionname <- function(team_id,                                    season = most_recent_wbb_season(),                                    ...) {   .espn_basketball_functionname(     league  = "womens-college-basketball",     team_id = team_id,     season  = season,     ...   ) }

title: CLAUDE.md – wehoop Development Guide
text: V2: Returns resultSets[].headers[] + rowSet[][] (tabular). Parsed via wnba_stats_map_result_sets(). V3: Returns nested JSON (e.g., game.actions[], boxScoreTraditional.homeTeam.players[]). Parsed via purrr::pluck() -> data.frame() -> pipeline. V3--V2 conversion pipeline (wnba_pbp() V3 path): wnba_playbyplayv3() -> .build_player_roster_wnba() -> .v3_to_v2_format_wnba() -> .players_on_court_v3_wnba(). Produces V2-compatible columns retaining V3-columns (x_legacy, y_legacy, shot_distance, shot_result, is_field_goal, points_total, shot_value). V3 PBP single personId per action (player1_id/player2_id/player3_id like V2). V3 substitutions: actionType="Substitution", personId=outgoing player, description contains “SUB: IncomingPlayer OutgoingPlayer”. V3 clock format: ISO 8601 duration "PT10M30.00S" ("MM:SS"). Parsed base R regexec()/regmatches(). V3 -court players: .players_on_court_v3_wnba() uses wnba_gamerotation() stint data interval mapping via findInterval().

title: CLAUDE.md – wehoop Development Guide
text: Every wrapper returns variable assigned inside tryCatch must initialize variable tryCatch block. Otherwise, API errors (500s, timeouts, HTTP/2 stream errors, connection resets) error handler runs, return variable never bound, return(<var>) throws object '<var>' found instead intended cli::cli_alert_danger + empty fallback. rule applies every return variable name, just df_list: plays_df, pbp, standings, teams, team_box_score, athlete_roster_df, games, conferences, resp, data, etc. Initialize appropriate empty value — list() named-list returns, NULL single-object returns, data.frame() tibble returns.
code: wnba_func <- function(...) {   endpoint <- wnba_endpoint('foo')   params   <- list(...)    df_list <- list()   # <-- MANDATORY. Not inside tryCatch.    tryCatch(     expr = {       resp    <- request_with_proxy(url = endpoint, params = params, ...)       df_list <- wnba_stats_map_result_sets(resp)     },     error = function(e) {       cli::cli_alert_danger("{Sys.time()}: Invalid arguments or no data available!")       cli::cli_alert_danger("Error:\n{e}")     },     warning = function(w) {       cli::cli_alert_warning("{Sys.time()}: Warning:\n{w}")     },     finally = {}   )   return(df_list) }

title: CLAUDE.md – wehoop Development Guide
text: WNBA Stats API ESPN’s JSON payloads add columns time without removing old ones, occasionally rename drop columns. Two guardrails apply: Inside functions — dropping known-transient column, use dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("colname")) instead dplyr::select(-"colname"). bare form errors moment upstream drops column; any_of -ops silently. Inside pipelines rename — use dplyr::rename(dplyr::any_of(c(new = "old"))) schema drift removes old survivable. See espn_wbb_conferences() ncaa_wbb_NET_rankings() examples.

title: CLAUDE.md – wehoop Development Guide
text: .retry_request() resolves proxy order: Explicit proxy = argument (caller-supplied; highest precedence). getOption("wehoop.proxy") session-level fallback — set options(wehoop.proxy = ...) every call picks . http_proxy / https_proxy / no_proxy environment variables — libcurl reads automatically explicit proxy supplied. proxy value (whether passed read option) accepts: - "http://host:port" — string form, forwarded httr2::req_proxy(url = ...). - list(url = "...", port = 8080, username = "...", password = "...", auth = "basic") — spread keyword args httr2::req_proxy() authenticated proxies. Per-call override works wrappers thread ... request_with_proxy() — ’s every WNBA Stats API function (wnba_*()), e.g. wnba_pbp(game_id = "...", proxy = "http://-proxy:8080"). ESPN / NCAA / KenPom wrappers call .retry_request() directly without ..., use options() fallback env-var path. session option recommended pattern working one proxy across many calls — ’s single line top script covers everything.

title: CLAUDE.md – wehoop Development Guide
text: Always use subset direction column assertions. upstream APIs add columns, strict expect_equal break new column. rule : expected list must subset actual columns. Anti-patterns avoid: dynamic columns, expect_true((core_cols %% colnames(x))) equivalent subset-direction expect_in(). Per-element null checks: API sometimes returns fewer result sets test expects (e.g., 7 instead 11), use inline helper individual asserts skip gracefully rather erroring: See test-wnba_teamvsplayer.R test-wnba_playerdashboardbyclutch.R live examples.
code: test_that("WNBA Endpoint Name", {   skip_on_cran()   skip_on_ci()   skip_wnba_stats_test()  # Requires WNBA_STATS_TESTS=1    x <- wnba_function(game_id = "1022200034")    # Skip-if-empty guard — always right after the API call, before any assertions   # that touch x[[1]]. Handles transient 500s and HTTP/2 stream errors.   if (length(x) == 0 || is.null(x[[1]]) || !is.data.frame(x[[1]]) ||       nrow(x[[1]]) == 0) {     skip("No rows returned from endpoint at test time")   }    cols_x1 <- c("col1", "col2", ...)   expect_in(sort(cols_x1), sort(colnames(x[[1]])))   # expected ⊆ actual   expect_s3_class(x[[1]], "data.frame")    Sys.sleep(3)  # Rate limiting between tests }) # WRONG - flags when upstream adds a column, even though it's non-breaking expect_equal(sort(colnames(x[[1]])), sort(cols_x1))  # WRONG - same direction problem, just phrased with expect_in expect_in(sort(colnames(x[[1]])), sort(cols_x1)) check_cols <- function(i, cols) {   if (length(x) < i || is.null(x[[i]]) || !is.data.frame(x[[i]]) ||       ncol(x[[i]]) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))   expect_in(sort(cols), sort(colnames(x[[i]])))   expect_s3_class(x[[i]], "data.frame") } check_cols(1, cols_x1) check_cols(2, cols_x2)

title: CLAUDE.md – wehoop Development Guide
text: Quarter length: 10 minutes (12 like NBA) Regulation time: 40 minutes total (48) Overtime: 5 minutes (NBA) Game ID format: Start “10” (e.g., "1022200034") LeagueID: “10” WNBA endpoints Base URL: https://stats.wnba.com/stats/{endpoint} Time calculations: 600 seconds per quarter (720), 2400 total regulation seconds (2880)

title: CLAUDE.md – wehoop Development Guide
text: Three files describe release different audiences. Whenever add NEWS.md bullet, think three committing: NEWS.md — authoritative changelog downstream users; rendered pkgdown changelog. new bullets go recent unreleased version heading (currently # **wehoop 3.0.0**). create new version section ahead release. Add extend existing subsection (### Bug fixes, ### Deprecations, ### Test infrastructure, etc.) instead starting new one change incremental. 3.0.0 ships CRAN, development version gets heading rule rolls forward. cran-comments.md — gets submitted CRAN. Every behavioral user-visible change add NEWS.md also reflected cran-comments.md submission. two files duplicates: NEWS.md long-form changelog, cran-comments.md short-form release summary. NEWS.md bullet purely internal (refactor, test infrastructure, dev tooling) can omitted cran-comments.md. _pkgdown.yml — pkgdown reference index. New exported functions need land right reference: section. existing wehoop config uses starts_with("wnba_") / starts_with("espn_") / starts_with("ncaa_") selectors new functions matching prefixes picked automatically; explicitly-listed functions need manual entry. Functions deprecated via lifecycle::deprecate_stop() + @keywords internal excluded rendered index default — preview pkgdown::build_site() doubt. change touches API surface (new export, deprecation, removal), include one-line note commit message confirming ’ve checked three files.

title: CLAUDE.md – wehoop Development Guide
text: Use Conventional Commits: Prefer scoped commit subjects useful (e.g., feat(pbp): ..., docs(instructions): ...). Use type!: BREAKING CHANGE: footer breaking changes. Split unrelated work separate commits reviewability. Important: Never include AI agents assistants (e.g., Claude, Copilot) co-authors commits. Omit Co-Authored-trailers referencing AI tools.

title: CLAUDE.md – wehoop Development Guide
text: pad_id() must called game IDs passing API (zero-pads 10 digits). Always initialize df_list <- list() tryCatch blocks. ESPN API columns change time – use subset validation tests. V3 endpoints return different structures per endpoint – always verify. data.frame(list_of_items) can produce unexpected column types API returns mixed NULL/value fields – use %||% defaults. WNBA uses 10-minute quarters 40-minute regulation – time calculations differ NBA. Local dev artifacts (e.g., .vscode, .claude) can surface R CMD check notes. Never hand-edit NAMESPACE files man/; regenerate devtools::document().

what: A note on the API surface
title: ESPN basketball endpoints -- WBB & WNBA
text: ESPN exposes basketball data three public, unauthenticated API hosts, wehoop reaches : site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/basketball/{league} stable. serves scoreboards, teams, rosters, schedules, news, injuries, standings, player team season stats. sports.core.api.espn.com/v2/sports/basketball/{league} carries deeper resources: athlete indexes, per-event detail (odds, win probabilities, officials, broadcasts), seasons, venues, coaches, WNBA draft, transactions. Big collections paginate via $ref links. site.web.api.espn.com/apis/common/v3/sports/basketball/{league} carries per-athlete deep detail – season overview, stats category, game--game logs, situational splits. ’s least stable three; older seasons sometimes return 404, every athlete represented. ’s fourth host (cdn.espn.com/core) surfaces information site-v2 /summary endpoint already parse, don’t wrap . league slugs URL paths womens-college-basketball wnba. matter ’re building requests hand. Rate limits. ESPN doesn’t publish . practice, requests arriving faster one per second occasionally come back HTTP 429 silently empty payloads. ’re looping many games athletes, drop Sys.sleep(1) calls. Proxies. ESPN wrappers don’t accept per-call proxy = argument; call package’s HTTP layer directly. Set proxy top session options(wehoop.proxy = "http://host:port") (list, authenticated proxies) every ESPN call pick automatically.

title: ESPN basketball endpoints -- WBB & WNBA
text: athlete endpoints deepest part surface. Pull roster, pick player, biographical data, season-level totals, per-game log, situational splits, awards history keyed athlete_id. Everything works WNBA side – swap espn_wbb_* espn_wnba_* use WNBA athlete_id (’ja Wilson "3149391"). things know athlete endpoints: espn_*_athlete_eventlog() returns $ref URL columns rather parsed game stats. Reach espn_*_athlete_gamelog() want per-game numbers tibble form. espn_*_athlete_awards() sparse. Many athletes ESPN-recorded awards, empty tibble normal. web-common-v3 endpoints (_athlete_overview, _athlete_stats, _athlete_gamelog, _athlete_splits) less stable rest surface. seasons roughly 2018 return HTTP 404, every athlete index.
code: library(dplyr)  uconn_roster <- espn_wbb_team_roster(team_id = 2509, season = 2025)  athlete_id   <- uconn_roster$athlete_id[1] athlete_name <- uconn_roster$athlete_display_name[1] message("Selected: ", athlete_name, " (", athlete_id, ")")  # Bio and profile bio <- espn_wbb_athlete_info(athlete_id = athlete_id) glimpse(bio)  # Season overview (web-common-v3) overview <- espn_wbb_athlete_overview(   athlete_id = athlete_id, season = 2025 ) names(overview)  # Game-by-game log gamelog <- espn_wbb_athlete_gamelog(   athlete_id = athlete_id, season = 2025 ) head(gamelog[, c("game_date", "opponent", "points", "rebounds", "assists")])  # Situational splits (home/away, by month, vs ranked, ...) splits <- espn_wbb_athlete_splits(   athlete_id = athlete_id, season = 2025 ) head(splits)

title: ESPN basketball endpoints -- WBB & WNBA
text: combination _pbp() _event_probabilities() quickest way chart game’s momentum. Event '401736171' 2024 WNBA regular-season game. can layer scoring plays pbp label momentum swings, join _event_officials() _event_broadcasts() want contextual annotations. ESPN doesn’t carry betting lines NCAA games, espn_wbb_event_odds() always returns empty tibble. function exists API symmetry; ’s bug. Win probabilities, officials, broadcasts populated leagues.
code: library(wehoop) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2)  game_id <- "401736171"  pbp   <- espn_wnba_pbp(game_id = game_id) probs <- espn_wnba_event_probabilities(event_id = game_id, limit = 200)  plot_data <- probs %>%   mutate(seq = as.integer(sequence_number)) %>%   arrange(seq)  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = seq, y = as.numeric(home_win_percentage))) +   geom_line(color = "#221A4D", linewidth = 0.8) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +   labs(     title = paste("Win probability --", game_id),     x = "Play sequence",     y = "Home team win probability"   ) +   theme_minimal() # Pre-game odds (populated when ESPN carries lines) odds <- espn_wnba_event_odds(event_id = game_id)  # Officials officials <- espn_wnba_event_officials(event_id = game_id) officials[, c("full_name", "position")]  # Broadcast outlets broadcasts <- espn_wnba_event_broadcasts(event_id = game_id) broadcasts[, c("market", "names")]

what: Working with the WNBA draft and transactions
title: ESPN basketball endpoints -- WBB & WNBA

code: # 2025 WNBA draft picks draft_2025 <- espn_wnba_draft(season = 2025) head(draft_2025[, c("pick", "round", "team_name", "athlete_display_name")])  # Recent transactions (waivers, trades, signings) txn <- espn_wnba_transactions(season = 2025, limit = 100) head(txn[, c("date", "type", "athlete_display_name", "team_name")])  # Free agents -- empty outside the FA window, which is roughly # January through April each year fa <- espn_wnba_freeagents(season = 2025) nrow(fa)

text: Sometimes don’t specific team athlete mind – want league-wide leaderboard, every venue, every coach, full athlete index. catalog endpoints cover . athlete index largest catalog endpoints – expect 6,000+ rows recent WBB season. Pagination handled internally, exploratory pulls ’ll usually want small limit. seasons catalog mostly handy want know years ESPN record start multi-season pull.
code: # Statistical leaders (points, rebounds, assists, ...) wnba_ldrs <- espn_wnba_leaders(season = 2024, season_type = 2) head(wnba_ldrs)  # Every WNBA arena ESPN tracks wnba_venues <- espn_wnba_venues() head(wnba_venues[, c("full_name", "city", "state", "capacity")])  # Coaches (current season) wbb_coaches <- espn_wbb_coaches(season = 2025) head(wbb_coaches[, c("full_name", "team_name", "experience")]) # WNBA -- a couple hundred active players wnba_athletes <- espn_wnba_athletes_index(   season = 2025, active = TRUE, limit = 5000 ) nrow(wnba_athletes) head(wnba_athletes[, c("display_name", "position_name", "team_name")])  # WBB -- cap at 50 rows just to peek; the default limit is 25,000 wbb_athletes <- espn_wbb_athletes_index(season = 2025, limit = 50) head(wbb_athletes[, c("display_name", "position_name", "team_name")]) wnba_seasons <- espn_wnba_seasons() head(wnba_seasons[, c("year", "start_date", "end_date")])  # Single-season metadata is mostly $ref URLs to sub-resources, so # espn_*_seasons() is usually the more useful starting point wnba_s2025 <- espn_wnba_season_info(season = 2025)

title: ESPN basketball endpoints -- WBB & WNBA
text: endpoints exist ESPN deliberately wrapped: handful endpoints wrap known data quirks: espn_wbb_injuries() espn_wbb_team_injuries() – ESPN rarely populates injury data college basketball. espn_wbb_event_odds() – always empty; ESPN doesn’t carry NCAA lines. espn_wnba_freeagents() – empty outside FA window. espn_*_athlete_awards() – sparse athletes. espn_*_athlete_eventlog() – returns $ref URLs, parsed stats. Use _athlete_gamelog() instead. espn_*_season_info() – mostly $ref URLs. web-common-v3 endpoints – legacy seasons return HTTP 404. something looks , empty tibble far often correct, expected return bug. ESPN’s basketball coverage uneven across leagues, seasons, franchise tenures, wehoop mirrors unevenness honestly rather papering .

what: A note on rate limits and proxies
title: Getting Started with wehoop
text: ESPN WNBA Stats API don’t publish official rate limits, practice return HTTP 429s silent empty responses hammer . ’re looping hundreds game IDs: Add Sys.sleep(1) (ESPN) Sys.sleep(3) (WNBA Stats API) calls. Wrap loop tryCatch() single transient failure doesn’t halt whole job. ’re behind corporate proxy, set per session every wehoop call route : WNBA Stats API wrappers also accept per-call proxy = argument takes precedence option.

title: wehoop Copilot Instructions
text: Follow tidyverse style: snake_case variables/functions, 2-space indentation. WNBA Stats API functions use request_with_proxy() HTTP calls required WNBA headers. Use %||% (rlang) null-safe defaults parsing API responses. returned data frames must pass janitor::clean_names() make_wehoop_data(). Use pad_id() game IDs passing API. Internal/non-exported helpers prefixed . (e.g., .players_on_court_v3_wnba()). Keep imports minimal explicit; remove unused imports.

title: wehoop Copilot Instructions
text: WNBA Stats HTTP requests use request_with_proxy() utils_wnba_stats.R handles required WNBA headers: - Origin: https://stats.wnba.com - Referer: https://www.wnba.com/ .retry_request() resolves proxy order: explicit proxy = arg → getOption("wehoop.proxy") → libcurl env vars (http_proxy / https_proxy / no_proxy). Proxy value accepts URL string "http://host:port" named list list(url=, port=, username=, password=, auth=) spread httr2::req_proxy(). Per-call override (wnba_foo(proxy = ...)) threads WNBA Stats wrappers (forward ... request_with_proxy). ESPN / NCAA / KenPom wrappers call .retry_request() directly without ..., use options(wehoop.proxy = ...) session top — ’s recommended pattern session runs proxy. Shared internal helpers utils.R: - check_status() HTTP response validation - make_wehoop_data() standardizing data frame output - pad_id() zero-padding game IDs ESPN live endpoints use rvest::session() httr::timeout().

text: Every exported function needs: @name @rdname tags NULL object @title bold markdown description @author tag @param every parameter descriptive text @return markdown tables documenting column names types data frame returned @importFrom specific function imports @export @family grouping pkgdown (e.g., “WNBA PBP Functions”, “ESPN WBB Functions”) ESPN wrappers (espn_wbb_*, espn_wnba_*): use standard @examples block wrapped \donttest{} (live-API examples). add @details code blocks. WNBA Stats API NCAA wrappers (wnba_*, ncaa_wbb_*): preserve legacy @details--fenced-code-block convention wehoop 2.x backward compatibility.

title: wehoop Copilot Instructions
text: Use skip_on_cran() skip_on_ci() guards live API tests. Add source-specific env-var skip helper immediately skip_on_ci(): skip_wnba_stats_test() test-wnba_*.R skip_espn_test() test-espn_wbb_*.R test-espn_wnba_*.R skip_ncaa_wbb_test() test-ncaa_wbb_*.R helpers live tests/testthat/helper-skip.R gate env vars (WNBA_STATS_TESTS=1, ESPN_TESTS=1, NCAA_WBB_TESTS=1). Column assertions must always use subset direction — expected ⊆ actual: expect_in(sort(expected_cols), sort(colnames(x))). WNBA ESPN APIs add columns without removing old ones, strict expect_equal(sort(colnames(x)), sort(cols)) flag new column. subset direction pattern survives upstream drift. Always add skip--empty guard immediately API call, assertion touches x[[1]]: handles transient 500s, HTTP/2 stream errors, empty responses without polluting failure report. tests assert multiple result sets (x[[1]]..x[[N]]) API sometimes returns fewer elements, wrap assertion per-index null/empty-column helper: See test-wnba_teamvsplayer.R test-wnba_playerdashboardbyclutch.R. dynamic columns, expect_true((core_cols %% colnames(x))) equivalent subset-direction expect_in(). Add Sys.sleep(3) end WNBA Stats API tests rate limiting. Test game ID: "1022200034" known completed WNBA games.
code: x <- wnba_func(...) if (length(x) == 0 || is.null(x[[1]]) || !is.data.frame(x[[1]]) ||     nrow(x[[1]]) == 0) {   skip("No rows returned from endpoint at test time") } check_cols <- function(i, cols) {   if (length(x) < i || is.null(x[[i]]) || !is.data.frame(x[[i]]) ||       ncol(x[[i]]) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))   expect_in(sort(cols), sort(colnames(x[[i]])))   expect_s3_class(x[[i]], "data.frame") }

text: Two regeneration steps part commit workflow whenever relevant sources change. mechanical — never edit generated regions hand. Markdown TOCs. NEWS.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/pull_request_template.md carry doctoc-generated TOC inside marker comments. (cran-comments.md intentionally excluded — short CRAN-submission file.) editing , run: tools/run_doctoc.R -deps R replacement npm doctoc CLI; idempotent runs without Node.js. Use --maxlevel 2 (level-3 sub-entries crowd nav). README.md. Rendered README.Rmd (output: github_document: { toc: true, toc_depth: 2 }). editing Rmd, run devtools::build_readme() commit README.Rmd + README.md together. Never hand-edit README.md. DESCRIPTION. editing DESCRIPTION (deps, versions, Authors@R, etc.), run usethis::use_tidy_description() normalize field order, alphabetize Imports/Suggests, reflow long lines. Run even one-line edits. Release notes triad — NEWS.md / cran-comments.md / _pkgdown.yml. Whenever add NEWS.md bullet, check two: NEWS.md — new bullets go recent unreleased version heading (currently # **wehoop 3.0.0**). create new version section ahead release; extend existing subsections (### Bug fixes, ### Deprecations, ### Test infrastructure, …). release ships rule rolls forward next dev version. cran-comments.md — every user-visible / behavioral change NEWS.md reflected cran-comments.md submission. Internal-changes (refactors, test infra, dev tooling) can omitted. _pkgdown.yml — new exports go right reference: section. starts_with() selectors auto-pick wnba_* / espn_* / ncaa_* prefixes; explicitly-listed functions need manual entry. lifecycle::deprecate_stop() + @keywords internal excludes function rendered index default.

title: wehoop Copilot Instructions
text: V3 endpoints return nested JSON – use purrr::pluck() extraction. V3 PBP clock format "PT10M30.00S" "MM:SS". Parsed base R regexec()/regmatches(). V3 PBP substitutions: personId = outgoing player, incoming parsed “SUB: IncomingPlayer OutgoingPlayer” description. V3--V2 conversion pipeline (wnba_pbp() V3 path): wnba_playbyplayv3() -> .build_player_roster_wnba() -> .v3_to_v2_format_wnba() -> .players_on_court_v3_wnba(). .players_on_court_v3_wnba() uses wnba_gamerotation() stint data interval mapping (substitution-event parsing like V2). V3 boxscore endpoints namespace: boxscoretraditionalv3, boxscoreadvancedv3, boxscoreusagev3, boxscoresummaryv3, etc.

title: wehoop Copilot Instructions
text: Quarter length: 10 minutes (12 like NBA) Regulation time: 40 minutes total (48) Overtime: 5 minutes (NBA) Game ID format: Start “10” (e.g., "1022200034") LeagueID: “10” WNBA endpoints Base URL: https://stats.wnba.com/stats/{endpoint} Time calculations: Use 600 seconds per quarter (720), 2400 seconds regulation (2880)

title: wehoop Copilot Instructions
text: Return-value initialization mandatory: every wrapper return(X) X assigned inside tryCatch(expr = {...}) must initialize X tryCatch. Otherwise, API errors, return(X) throws object 'X' found instead intended empty-list fallback. Applies df_list, plays_df, pbp, teams, standings, conferences, resp, games, data, etc. — return variable. dropping known-transient column inside function, use dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("colname")) instead dplyr::select(-"colname"). bare form errors moment upstream drops column. renaming columns janitor::clean_names(), use dplyr::rename(dplyr::any_of(c(new = "old"))) function survives upstream rename/drops without breaking. ESPN API columns change time — column assertions tests must use subset direction (expect_in(expected, actual)). V3 endpoints return different structures per endpoint — verify response structure. pad_id() must called game IDs passing API. Local editor/worktree artifacts (e.g., .vscode, .claude, tools/, temp logs) can cause R CMD check notes — add .Rbuildignore. Never edit NAMESPACE man/ files hand; regenerate devtools::document(). WNBA time calculations use 10-minute quarters (600 seconds/quarter, 2400 seconds regulation) — NBA 12-minute / 720-second / 2880-second constants. old .players_on_court() helper wnba_stats_pbp.R bug corrected 3.0.0.

title: Build/update wehoop WBB play-by-play database — update_wbb_db
text: function creates updates data table name tblname within SQLite database (drivers via db_connection) located dbdir named dbname. data table combines play play data every available game back 2002 season adds recent completed games soon available wehoop. argument force_rebuild hybrid type. can rebuild play play data table either whole wehoop era (force_rebuild = TRUE) just specified seasons (e.g. force_rebuild = c(2019, 2020)). Please note following behavior: force_rebuild = TRUE: data table name tblname removed completely rebuilt scratch. helpful new columns added -Season. force_rebuild = c(2019, 2020): data table name tblname preserved rows 2019 2020 seasons deleted re-added. intended used ongoing seasons ESPN's data provider can make changes underlying data week. parameter db_connection intended advanced users want use DBI drivers, MariaDB, Postgres odbc. Please note arguments dbdir dbname dropped case db_connection provided argument tblname still used write data table database.

what: @return column descriptions on every exported function
title: wehoop 3.0.0
text: Every @return markdown table across 42 R source files upgraded two columns (col_name | types) three columns (col_name | types | description). 580+ tables touched 4,341 total table rows; every result set every function now ships per-column description ?<function> help, pkgdown reference, rendered man pages. Existing prose \describe{} blocks (notably load_wbb_pbp(), load_wnba_pbp(), parameter_descriptions) unchanged. Coverage — frequency-weighted, ?fn readers actually see — 74.7% 4,341 @return table rows now carry hand-quality description (curated + ESPN-API + mined). remaining 25.3% heuristic-fallback rows; heuristic generator’s snake_case expansion + suffix rules cover acceptably (e.g. defended_at_rim_field_goals_attempted → “Number defended rim field goals attempted.”), long tail dominated single-occurrence columns low-traffic endpoints. Description sources (precedence order, first match wins): tools/docs/column_descriptions_curated.csv — 619 hand-authored entries focused highest-traffic columns basketball / ESPN domain conventions (team identity, advanced shooting metrics, hustle stats, V2 vs V3 column pairs, ESPN athlete / event / news fields). tools/docs/column_descriptions_api.csv — 181 ESPN-authored descriptions mined live 14 endpoints per league across wnba womens-college-basketball, covering 9 endpoint families: core-v2 athlete statistics (per-season, post-season, career), core-v2 team statistics, core-v2 statisticslog, core-v2 leaders, web-v3 athlete stats / splits / gamelog / overview, web-v3 statistics/byathlete leaderboards. Three response shapes recognized: nested categories stats objects, parallel arrays categories, top-level parallel-array shapes (splits / gamelog). covers ESPN stat-section column families (general_*, offensive_*, defensive_*, rebounding_*, shooting_*, misc_*) full prose definitions straight ESPN — e.g. defensive_blocks → “Short blocked shot, number times defensive player legally deflects field goal attempt offensive player.” Re-mine time Rscript tools/docs/mine_api_descriptions.R. Mined \item{...}{...} lines existing \describe{} blocks. Heuristic patterns driven column-name suffixes (*_id, *_pct, *_made, *_attempted, *_per_36, etc.) basketball-friendly noun substitution (fg → field goals, tov → turnovers, oreb → offensive rebounds). New tooling tools/docs/ (.Rbuildignore’d, sibling existing tools/probes/ diagnostic toolkit): sweep idempotent: re-running augment_all_r_files() updating dictionary refreshes existing 3-column tables place rather appending fourth column.

title: wehoop 3.0.0
text: Jittered exponential backoff .retry_request(). Replaced default fixed 2-second retry cadence runif(1, 0.5, 1.5) * 2^retries concurrent users hitting rate-limited endpoint don’t synchronize thundering-herd burst Cloudflare scores attack. 3 max tries; backoff envelope (~0.5–6s); just spread. Restored proxy support. wehoop migrated httr httr2 V3 work, legacy httr::use_proxy() plumbing dropped request_with_proxy() quietly stopped honoring proxies (... preserved purely source compatibility). request_with_proxy() lower-level .retry_request() now accept proxy = argument: proxy = NULL (default) — libcurl reads http_proxy / https_proxy / no_proxy env vars automatically. proxy = "http://host:port" — string form, forwarded httr2::req_proxy(url = ...). proxy = list(url=, port=, username=, password=, auth=) — named list spread httr2::req_proxy() authenticated proxies. Resolution order .retry_request(): explicit proxy = arg → getOption("wehoop.proxy") → libcurl env vars. ... thread works WNBA Stats wrappers (forward request_with_proxy()); ESPN / NCAA wrappers call .retry_request() directly without ..., use options(wehoop.proxy = ...) top session cover without per-function plumbing. Validated end--end: ncaa_wbb_teams() espn_wnba_game_all() routed authenticated test proxy via option fallback.

title: wehoop 3.0.0
text: Empty / NULL responses now FAIL test instead silently SKIPping. earlier skip("rows returned endpoint test time") guard hiding regressions: upstream endpoint starts returning HTML (404 / maintenance) breaks silent way, test flag . Converted 117 guards across tests/testthat/test-*.R skip(...) fail(...) + return(invisible(NULL)) test surfaces FAIL count follow-. Deprecation skips env-gated skip_*_test() / skip_on_cran() / skip_on_ci() helpers unchanged. Pinned 16 wnba_team* test files most_recent_wnba_season() most_recent_wnba_season() - 1 team-stats endpoints known-completed season query don’t degenerate “rows” WNBA -season window. wnba_teams() standings tests still track live season ’s ’re meant verify. Bumped .ncaa_headers() user-agent Chrome 130 added Sec-Fetch-* / sec-ch-ua-* headers real browser sends. ncaa_wbb_teams() keeps legacy stats.ncaa.org/team/inst_team_list scrape (per-season per-division team list season_id populated), now threads proxy = argument ... .retry_request() top level. stats.ncaa.org fronted Akamai returns HTTP 403 (Reference #18.<...>) many residential cloud IP ranges; pass proxy egresses non-blocked address — either per-call (ncaa_wbb_teams(year, division, proxy = list(url=, port=, username=, password=))) session-wide (options(wehoop.proxy = list(...))). See Network access section ?ncaa_wbb_teams full resolution order.
